title: Maintaining Proper Drain Line Slope
description: Correct pitch is critical when installing horizontal drainage lines to guarantee that waste solids and liquids travel together efficiently toward the main sewer. If a pipe lacks adequate slope, wastewater flow slows down, causing suspended solids to settle at the bottom and create chronic blockages. Conversely, an excessively steep angle can cause liquids to drain too quickly, leaving heavy waste behind. Always verify pitch requirements against your local building and plumbing codes, maintain consistent support with proper pipe hangers to avoid low spots or bellies, and check alignment using a precision level during rough-in.

Maintaining Proper Drain Line Slope

Correct pitch is critical when installing horizontal drainage lines to guarantee that waste solids and liquids travel together efficiently toward the main sewer. If a pipe lacks adequate slope, wastewater flow slows down, causing suspended solids to settle at the bottom and create chronic blockages. Conversely, an excessively steep angle can cause liquids to drain too quickly, leaving heavy waste behind. Always verify pitch requirements against your local building and plumbing codes, maintain consistent support with proper pipe hangers to avoid low spots or bellies, and check alignment using a precision level during rough-in.
